subject: MSA security exhibit: pen-test carveouts, SOC 2 assertions, and evidence bundles
messages_1_subject: Initial assurance asks + redline checklist for MSA
messages_1_body:
Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. We've started a quick sweep of the MSA and the Order Form and flagged a few items in the security exhibit we need clarified before legal signs off. The main asks from our side: a narrow pen-test window (we prefer a 48h notice with 5 business day staging access), SOC 2 assertions and date of last report, and an evidence delivery plan for the items that map to our privacy questionnaire.

I've attached a short checklist (PHT_AuditChecklist.xlsx) that maps requested evidence to the MSA sections — it's our standard intake. Two specific callouts: 
- Mutuality language around inspection scope: we need a clearer carveout for scheduled penetration tests vs. emergency forensic access.
- Retention and redaction: we requested an example of the ‘proof bundles’ you would deliver when customers request artifact-level evidence.

Can you route this to your legal and security teams and let us know the expected handback cadence? If possible, we'd like to close this before the week is out.

Regards,
Maya Patel
Sr. Contracts Manager
Pioneer HealthTech

Attachment: PHT_AuditChecklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
messages_2_subject: Re: Initial assurance asks + redline checklist for MSA
messages_2_body:
Hi Maya — thanks for the checklist and the clear priorities. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (sales ops) to scope a concise response. Quick answers up front: 

1) Pen-test windowing: we can accept a scheduled 48-hour notice for standard vendor or customer-led penetration tests; we'll add an emergency forensic access carveout limited to incident response with an SLA for notice to customers.

2) SOC 2: our latest SOC 2 Type II report is 2026-05 and we can provide a copy under NDA or via our secure evidence portal.

3) Evidence bundles: we use a tagging schema that groups artifacts by assertion (e.g., CC3-Access, CC7-Change) and produce a single PDF/manifest per request; we can share a sample bundle.

Action items from our side:
- Laura: audit the MSA security exhibit and propose redline text for the pen-test carveout and evidence delivery clause. Please highlight any risk we shouldn't accept.
- Ben: I'll work with you on mutual action plan timing and final order form attachments.

We can do a 30-min call later today if you'd prefer to walk line-by-line. Otherwise I'll send a tracked redline by end of day.

Best,
Logan
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

messages_3_subject: Re: Initial assurance asks + redline checklist for MSA
messages_3_body:
Logan / Maya — I reviewed the checklist and drafted targeted redlines to keep the MSA practical while preserving our platform protections. Summary of legal positions: 

• Pen-test carveouts: propose language that distinguishes (a) scheduled, customer-authorized testing (48h notice; staging environment; limited to non-prod unless a signed SLA allows prod testing), (b) vendor-conducted security assessments, and (c) emergency/forensic access for incident response (requires documented incident declaration; our on-call will coordinate access and sampling). We avoid open-ended inspection rights that would allow broad, continuous access.

• Evidence delivery (proof bundles): we will provide assertion-mapped artifacts and a manifest within 10 business days of a formal request; for high-sensitivity artifacts (logs, raw DB extracts) we will offer sanitized, sampled outputs or a certified attestation instead. This preserves confidentiality and limits exposure.

• SOC 2 and attestations: we'll include a representation of the latest report date and a mutual NDA requirement for artifact-level delivery. For recurring requests, propose a quarterly evidence window to avoid churning ops.

I attached the tracked MSA redline (MSA_redline_v3.docx) with inline comments where we need commercial input (notably: whether Pioneer will accept sampled logs vs. full exports and if they require a dedicated staging environment).

If acceptable to Pioneer, I recommend we: 
1) Agree the evidence types (full, sampled, attestation) for each checklist row.
2) Lock an initial pen-test week in the MAP and define an ops runbook for staging access.
3) Add an explicit limitation on audit frequency (e.g., 2 full evidence requests per 12 months per account) with carveouts for security incidents.

Happy to take questions on any line. If Pioneer can confirm appetite for sampled artifacts, I can finalize redlines for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.docx (tracked changes)
messages_4_subject: Re: Initial assurance asks + redline checklist for MSA
messages_4_body:
Thanks Laura — that reads pragmatic and addresses our concerns at a high level. A few clarifications from Pioneer side: 

• Sampled artifacts are acceptable for logs and operational telemetry as long as the sampling methodology is documented and reproducible.
• For scheduling: Pioneer can accept quarterly evidence windows and one additional ad-hoc request in case of a security incident.

Next steps from our side: I'll update the checklist to reflect sampled vs. full for each row and send a 30-min slot for a handshake call (we're available 10:30–11:00 PT or 3:00–3:30 PT). We've also attached a short mutual action plan (Proposed_MAP.docx) with suggested dates for the pen-test staging week and the first evidence delivery.

If that aligns, we can route the redline to procurement and legal for final signoff and then kick a DocuSign envelope.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Best,
Maya

Attachment: Proposed_MAP.docx; OrderForm_Draft.pdf
